data.title: Logo
data.tagline: A brand mark used to identify an organization, product, or service
data.learningOutcome: You can choose a Logo variant for a background or width and distinguish the Logo's responsibility from the Header, Favicon, and App Icon.
data.description: A Logo can appear in a website header, mobile navigation, on a dark surface, or in promotional material through different variants, while its core identity stays consistent. It helps people recognize the brand; it does not own page navigation or browser-system icons.

learning.assumes: You have seen a brand mark in a website header and a narrow mobile navigation layout.
learning.outcome: You can choose a Logo variant for a background or width and distinguish the Logo's responsibility from the Header, Favicon, and App Icon.

distinctions.label: Header
distinctions.explanation: Logo is the brand mark; a Header is the top page region that organizes the Logo, navigation, and action entries.

distinctions.label: Favicon
distinctions.explanation: Logo identifies the brand in page content; a Favicon identifies the site in browser tabs, bookmarks, and history.

explanation.title: Wide and symbol forms fit different spaces
explanation.text: A desktop header can use a horizontal Logo, while a narrow navigation may need a symbol or compact form. Arrangement and color can change, but the core shape, proportion, and identity should remain recognizable.

explanation.title: Include the background and host area in testing
explanation.text: Light, dark, and crowded navigation widths affect contrast, cropping, and legibility. Verify the Logo in the real header, not only as an isolated image.

data.boundary: Logo is the brand identity itself; a Header is the page structure that hosts a Logo, navigation, and actions; a Favicon and App Icon serve specific browser and operating-system surfaces. Making a Logo smaller does not adapt it automatically for those system icons.

lessonPractice.title: A horizontal Logo crowds the navigation on a narrow screen. What should you do?

options.label: Use the defined compact or symbol Logo and verify it separately on narrow and dark surfaces
options.feedback: Correct. Logo variants can adapt to space while preserving recognition; do not delete the brand or turn it into a toolbar icon.

options.label: Keep shrinking the horizontal wordmark until it fits beside the navigation
options.feedback: If the text becomes unreadable, brand recognition has already failed; switch to an appropriate compact variant.

options.label: Replace the Logo entirely with a menu icon and make people infer the brand from navigation
options.feedback: A menu icon communicates the action of opening navigation and cannot replace the brand identity entry.

data.agentPrompt: Preserve the brand's core shape and choose suitable Logo variants for the desktop header, mobile navigation, and dark backgrounds. Verify that the Logo does not crowd navigation and remains recognizable, using separate screenshots. Do not change the Favicon or toolbar action icons as a side effect.
